consensus_summary: Week (shabua/heptad) primarily denotes a unit of seven, most commonly seven years in prophetic contexts such as Daniel 9, while more broadly symbolizing divine completeness and the creation-Sabbath cycle; ordinary seven-day usage also exists.
book_summary: A unit of seven, not necessarily seven days; Scripture applies it to days or years according to the scale being counted.
consensus_core_identification: heptad/unit of seven (days or years, especially prophetic years)
book_core_identification: unit of seven scalable to days or years
rationale: Both identify the core as a flexible heptad rather than a fixed seven-day period. Consensus details (Daniel years, creation pattern, completeness) are elaborations of the same referent the book states minimally; no replacement or boundary shift occurs.
strongest_objection: Consensus sometimes elevates creation-week symbolism or eschatological placement as primary, while the book stays strictly definitional.
